Extracting it names the concept once and gives the upcoming surcharge a hook.

All 15 still green. Refactor phase complete.

## Refactor Phase Report

**File:** `/home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-09-04_13-54-07_claim-office-example-mapping_v6.1.4-continuation-guard-cc_opus-5-no-thinking/src/claim-office.ts`

### Naming evaluation (done first)
- `itemSurcharges`, `quote`, `policyBasePremium`, `groupBasePremium`, `formsBlock`, `roundUpInMHPCOsFavour` — all fit their current purpose; kept.
- Renamed local `basePremium` → `policyBase` inside `quote`. With both a policy-level and an item-level "base premium" now in play, the bare name was ambiguous about which scope it meant (Rule 2).

### Refactorings applied
1. **Extracted `itemBasePremium(item)`** — the concept "base premium of a single item" was expressed inline as `BASE_PREMIUMS[item.type]`, duplicating the lookup that `groupBasePremium` performs. Now named once (Rule 3).
2. **Split `itemSurcharge(item)` out of `itemSurcharges(items)`** — separates *which modifiers apply to one item* from *summing across items*. The reduce body is now a pure addition with no embedded conditional.

### APP mass
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `itemSurcharges` (+ new helpers) | 18 | 21 |
| `quote` | 13 | 13 |
| **Total** | **31** | **34** |

Mass rose by 3 — the two extracted functions add bindings and invocations that the inlined version did not pay for. **Accepted deliberately: Rule 2 trumps APP.** The conditional (mass 4) moved out of the loop body into a named single-item rule, which is where the domain actually locates it — a surcharge is a property of an item, not of an iteration step.

### Note for the next cycle
This positions the upcoming tests well without implementing them: the enchantment ≥ 5 surcharge is a second clause inside `itemSurcharge`, and the "cursed item only" scoping test (line 163) is already structurally satisfied since `itemSurcharge` can only see one item at a time. The policy-scoped modifiers (loyalty, follow-up) belong alongside `firstInsuranceSurcharge` in `quote`, which currently applies its rate to `policyBase` directly — when the second and third policy modifiers arrive, that trio will likely want extracting into a `policyModifiers(policyBase, customer, contractIndex)` function. I did not do it now: with only one policy modifier present there is no duplication to remove yet, and speculative structure would violate Rule 4.
